learningObjectives: Explain the independent Quilyn API learning workflow from definitions and messages to automated assertions.
Prepare API knowledge, access and authorized Tosca tooling for practice.
Launch the currently documented ApiScan.exe independently of Commander without inferring licensing exemptions.
Distinguish scan results, transport success and verified business outcomes.

elements.text: These Quilyn notes use current primary documentation; they are not a transcript of the inaccessible Academy course. Original section counts, lesson counts, duration and historical Tosca version have not been verified.

elements.title: Learning goals
items: Scan a definition or message from a file or URI.
Inspect the endpoint, method, parameters, headers, authentication and payload.
Run messages and inspect the request and response.
Export and maintain automation artifacts, then verify expected business outcomes.

rows: Read the API contract, message format and transport semantics.
Import a supported definition or file and inspect its operations/messages.
Configure authorized credentials and valid data; inspect request and response.
Export selected messages and maintain mappings and assertions.
Check negative behavior and business results, not only an HTTP status.

elements.text: This sequence is independent guidance. It does not establish the original course syllabus, exercise count or certification requirements.

elements.description: Understand basic API and HTTP concepts and Tosca Modules/TestCases. Use a permitted test environment and the access and licenses required by your organization; exact Academy prerequisites were not accessible.

Current Tosca 2026.1 docs name ApiScan.exe in %COMMANDER_HOME% as the filesystem launch entry. Running independently of Commander does not establish that an arbitrary copied executable needs no installation, license or supporting files.

elements.text: In Commander, select API Testing > API Scan; the Modules menu also offers Scan Application > Non UI > API Scan.

elements.description: Confirm with your administrator that your account belongs to the cloud license server. This connection workflow is documented; a pop-up alone does not prove a single root cause.

elements.title: Connect to the configured cloud server
items: Open license configuration, then Setup > Change connection.
Choose Connect to Cloud hosted License Server and confirm.
Sign in with your Tricentis Support Hub credentials; use the default proxy option when your environment requires it.
Confirm successful connection; if it fails, inspect the error with your administrator rather than assuming every license problem is resolved.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Why test at the API boundary

elements.description: API requests can exercise a service without driving a graphical interface. A callable interface and usable test environment can permit testing before a UI is ready.

elements.title: Independent testing guidance
items: Test business behavior, authentication and invalid data at the service boundary.
Keep UI tests for behavior that exists in the interface; API tests do not replace that coverage.
Measure execution and maintenance costs in the actual environment; API tests are not universally faster or maintenance-free.
Re-scan and inspect changed artifacts; contracts, data and assertions still need maintenance.

elements.text: Consult the current Tricentis Academy enrollment page for official prerequisites, assessment rules and credentials. These independent notes do not certify a badge, points, exam structure or certificate entitlement.

examPitfalls.title: Inferring a licensing exemption from an independent launch
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating filesystem launch as proof that no installation or license is needed.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the documented ApiScan.exe entry and check access/licensing for the installed product; these sources do not establish a universal exemption.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing independent preparation with Academy prerequisites
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating an old syllabus or exercise count as a current enrollment requirement.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use current Academy enrollment information for formal requirements; API and Tosca basics remain useful practical preparation.

examPitfalls.title: Equating a scan or successful HTTP status with test completeness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming technical messages or a success status verify every business outcome.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure data and explicit assertions; retain UI coverage and inspect expected results and negative behavior.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which filesystem launch entry is documented for API Scan in Tosca 2026.1?

options.text: Only a Tosca Server administrator console.
ApiScan.exe in %COMMANDER_HOME%.
Any copied executable with guaranteed exemption from installation and licensing.
Only a browser URL.

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish a documented entry point from an unsupported licensing claim.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The current launch article names ApiScan.exe in %COMMANDER_HOME%. Independent launch does not prove an installation or licensing exemption.

optionExplanations.A: The launch article provides a local executable rather than requiring this console.
optionExplanations.B: This is the current documented filesystem entry point.
optionExplanations.C: The article does not establish that arbitrary copied executables run without supporting files or licensing.
optionExplanations.D: The documented launch routes include Commander and the filesystem.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which preparation helps you construct meaningful API tests in this independent learning workflow?

options.text: Understand the API contract, HTTP basics and Tosca Modules/TestCases.
Memorize only the color of the toolbar.
Assume all requests need no data or credentials.
Ignore expected business outcomes.

practiceQuiz.hint: Prepare to configure requests and verify responses.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API concepts and automation basics help you configure the documented message controls and define useful assertions; this does not certify formal Academy prerequisites.

optionExplanations.A: These concepts support request configuration and meaningful verification.
optionExplanations.B: Toolbar color does not define API behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Services can require credentials and particular input data.
optionExplanations.D: Business outcomes are needed to determine whether the behavior is correct.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why can API testing be useful before a graphical interface is available?

options.text: A callable service interface can be exercised without driving the UI.
API tests never need any test data.
An API cannot be tested until the UI is finished.
API tests replace the need for a QA team.

practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on the interface being exercised.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When the service interface and usable test environment exist, testing can target them directly without a graphical UI. This does not remove data, access or assertion requirements.

optionExplanations.A: The service boundary can be tested directly when it is available.
optionExplanations.B: Meaningful requests often need data and credentials.
optionExplanations.C: A graphical UI is not necessary for a callable service interface.
optionExplanations.D: Automation does not remove test design and verification responsibilities.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A request returns a success status. What is still necessary to verify the intended business behavior?

options.text: Assume every business rule passed.
Delete negative tests.
Check the expected response data and effects against explicit assertions.
Award the official course certificate.

practiceQuiz.hint: Transport success and business verification are separate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A success response alone does not validate every expected field or effect. Use explicit expected results; an Academy credential is unrelated.

optionExplanations.A: The status alone cannot establish every business outcome.
optionExplanations.B: Negative behavior can still require coverage.
optionExplanations.C: Expected results and explicit assertions verify the actual intent.
optionExplanations.D: A request result does not establish course completion or credential entitlement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which extension is absent from the documented API Scan file-format list (JSON, RAML, Text, WADL, WSDL, XML, XSD)?

options.text: JSON
WSDL
JPEG
XML

practiceQuiz.hint: Compare the supported definition/message formats with an image format.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented list includes JSON, RAML, Text, WADL, WSDL, XML and XSD; JPEG is not listed. This is not a claim about all possible API representation formats.

optionExplanations.A: JSON is in the stated supported file list.
optionExplanations.B: WSDL is in the stated supported file list.
optionExplanations.C: JPEG is not in this documented scan-input list.
optionExplanations.D: XML is in the stated supported file list.

quickRecap.value: Inspect contract → scan → configure → run → automate and assert.
API/HTTP and Tosca basics, authorized environment and appropriate access/licensing.
ApiScan.exe in %COMMANDER_HOME%; independent launch is not a certified licensing exemption.
Use the current Academy enrollment page; original counts and certification claims are unverified.
Check expected data and business effects; scan output or a success status is not complete verification.
